title: Page someone when a transaction stops finishing

blocks.text: Last month a server lost both of its sessions to an issuer call that never returned, and terminals reversed purchases for forty minutes before anyone looked at the log. Operations want a page the moment a transaction stops finishing, and not one page more.

Finish `poll` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/StuckWatch.java`. A monitor calls it every few seconds for the life of the server, with the TransactionManager's `getHead()` and `getTail()` and the time of the poll. It returns the id of a transaction that has been running for longer than the limit given to the constructor, or `-1`. The server is busy at lunchtime and almost silent at night, and the page has to be right at both. About ten lines in total.
The first test runs a real TransactionManager with two sessions, in which one purchase hangs in a participant until the test releases it. The others pass head and tail values directly.

cases.says: with a real TransactionManager, a transaction hung in a participant is named once it has been the oldest unfinished one for longer than the limit, and nothing is named after it finishes
when head equals tail nothing is running, so a tail that hasn't moved for hours is not a stuck transaction
a hung transaction is named even when no new transactions arrive and head stays where it is
the time is counted from when the current tail became the oldest, so a busy server whose tail keeps moving is never named

origin.section: 8.5 A Transaction That Never Ends Writes Nothing, and the Ones After It Show Where It Is

concepts: A transaction that never ends writes no event; tail stays at its id while it is the oldest unfinished one, whether or not head moves, and an idle server has tail equal to head.
